candidate_scientific_questions: [Untested] Does m173 V2 continue rising as EA decreases, or does the current predicted maximum near 1/1 represent a real local regime? Fixed-loading ratio contrasts distinguish continuation from decline; near-matched DCM 1,500/2,000 ul contrasts separately address plug sensitivity.

[Untested] Does m125's approximately +18 ml V2 solvent-volume effect at 1/1 extend to 150 ul sample? This missing contrast tests whether the smooth 1/1 response remains consistent where the measured 2/1 surface was irregular.

[Untested] Does m13 develop a genuine transition between 2/1 and 5/1, and does m107 retain its high V2 at greater loading? These questions test response shape after the measured failure of simple acetoacetate-family transfer.

[General chemical knowledge and untested explanations] Basic nitrogen can interact with acidic silanol sites; accessible alcohols and carboxylic acids can hydrogen-bond to silica. Surface protonation, acid association, solubility and nonlinear adsorption are possible explanations for m19 or m173, not measured mechanisms.

[Untested structural transfer] Spacer length and aromatic attachment may alter m205/m206 adsorption geometry. Pyridyl ketone m66 tests transfer from pyridyl ester m90; p-methylbenzyl alcohol m135 tests alcohol transfer beyond the naphthalene pair. Bulk HBD/HBA and LogP do not resolve these effects.

[General chemical knowledge and untested hypothesis] Beta-dicarbonyl tautomerism and intramolecular hydrogen bonding may affect m107, m13 and related compounds. Keto-form HBD counts do not capture every possible tautomer, but no tautomeric mechanism was measured.

possible_model_blind_spots: Molecule-by-ratio interactions may be transferred too broadly between related alcohols or acetoacetates. Opposite historical residual signs argue against universal donor or carbonyl corrections.
Shared condition features may insufficiently distinguish V1 onset from V2 completion, particularly under loading changes or in m173's broad measured interval.

Experimental variability or omitted covariates compete with chemical explanations. Identical m174 inputs at 704ba630f25fe7f20166 and 92bac523bed1042d6a75 differ by 4.679/5.929 ml; repeated m25 inputs differ much less. No universal noise level follows.

possible_learning_bottlenecks: [Inference] Tail labels may distort related molecules or adjacent ratios. m205/m206 and m107/m13 provide measured counterexamples. Contrasts separating molecule offsets from ratio slopes should be more efficient than repeatedly sampling extreme predictions.

[Inference] Weak predicted loading sensitivity may reflect feature scaling, representation, regularization or insufficient interaction data. The packet does not identify which explanation is responsible.

[Observed plus inference] Identical recorded m174 inputs differ by approximately 4.68/5.93 ml (704ba630f25fe7f20166, 92bac523bed1042d6a75). Missing covariates or experimental variability compete with deterministic response-surface explanations. Purposeful replication could clarify the m125 valley if an eligible matching record exists.

[ML prior] Matched contrasts identify local interactions; broader structural coverage tests transfer. Their value depends on Row frequency and measurement variability. Novelty, prediction scale and historical error alone do not determine expected accuracy gain.
coverage_or_redundancy_concerns: The supplied pool contains extensive familiar DCM/PE loading-solvent grids and exact duplicates. For example, m89 candidates 0141de34d99a6428ddd7 and f1bb0be6e913a5e26491 have identical recorded inputs. Compare molecule identity and all five condition fields; multiplicity represents Row frequency, not independent coverage.

Some legal candidates repeat observed inputs under another ID, including m92 10/1, sample 100 ul, EA 200 ul candidate ab1062a71079c605f750. Such measurements address variability rather than add a new recorded-input location.

m167, m147, m105, m160/m161 and several transition curves have substantial coverage. Unobserved m66, m36 and m119 offer interpretable transfer questions. Broader novel ketone, aldehyde, ether and halogenated grids remain exploration options, but novelty alone does not establish information value.

Overall Row accuracy also requires representative moderate-volume regions and systematic V1 errors. Adaptive historical errors overrepresent previously investigated neighborhoods; no unbiased Row error estimate or retrained performance measure is supplied.
